summary: A transmon qubit at $\omega_q = 2\pi \times 3.1$ GHz is readout using a millimeter-wave cavity at $\omega_r = 2\pi \times 34.7$ GHz with coupling rate $g = 2\pi \times 1.3$ GHz, achieving a large detuning ratio $\omega_r/\omega_q > 10$ that suppresses drive-induced unwanted state transitions. Measurement fidelity exceeds 99% with over 100 readout photons and no quantum-limited amplifier, with resilience demonstrated up to $1,000$ drive photons.
motivation: Drive-induced resonant state transitions limit readout fidelity in conventional circuit QED systems where cavity and qubit frequencies are comparable; operating with large frequency separation between readout and qubit can suppress these transitions while maintaining fast qubit gates and low thermal occupancy.
method: Floquet simulations and experiments on a transmon-cavity system probe drive-induced transitions by sweeping drive strength and frequency. The state is prepared, driven near the readout resonance with variable photon number, and multistate readout distinguishes transitions to higher transmon levels.
result: No resonant state transitions observed up to $\bar{n}_d \approx 1,000$ photons from either $|0\rangle$ or $|1\rangle$, with measurement fidelities $\mathcal{F}_{|0\rangle} = \mathcal{F}_{|1\rangle} = 0.992$ at $\bar{n}_r = 109$ and readout time $\tau_r = 780$ ns; measurement efficiency is 1.74% with system added noise $\bar{n}_{\mathrm{sys}} = 28$ photons.
